messages:
Elaine: quick heads-up — p99 decode latency spiked after the 1799989xxx deploy, started seeing regression around 1799991200. profiler shows host CPU dominated by request parsing/http2 overhead.

Elaine: profiler snippet:
```text
process=host-proxy
span=1799991203
p99_decode(ms)=300 (baseline 120)
hot= http2::decode 42% | parse_headers 18% | kv_cache_miss_handler 12%
syscalls= recvmsg x 1200 / request
```

Sanjay: can you paste the raw flame? small frames showing up?

Elaine: attaching inline summary — lots of tiny recv calls, frames <= 64B common. looks like tokenizer is emitting very small chunks which causes extra http2/frame overhead. Also seeing KV cache miss rate tick up when upstream frames are tiny.

Marc: hypothesis: host tokenization/streaming chunker splitting aggressively -> many tiny HTTP2 DATA frames -> CPU + context switch overhead + KV cache gets fragmented prefixes -> miss thrash.

Nina: i repro locally with synthetic workload that emits tokens at ~1 token/ms. baseline pipeline with chunk-coalesce disabled shows p99 ~320ms. enabling coalesce to 512B reduces p99 to ~115ms.

Ryan: what's the tradeoff? larger coalesce could add tail latency if we wait for more bytes.

Sanjay: idea — coalesce by bytes OR token boundary OR timeout (e.g., flush after 8ms or 256B). default should bias reduce frames without adding noticeable head-of-line delay.

Elaine: test matrix I ran (microbench):
- coalesce=64B, timeout=4ms => p99 280ms, cpu 18% up
- coalesce=256B, timeout=8ms => p99 118ms, cpu back to baseline
- coalesce=512B, timeout=12ms => p99 112ms, slight increase in tail for tiny requests (~+5ms)

Elaine: quick log showing KV miss correlation:
```text
request_id=abc123 frames=28 avg_frame_size=48 kv_miss_pct=23%
request_id=def456 frames=6  avg_frame_size=420 kv_miss_pct=3%
```

Marc: ok that matches: fragmentation -> more distinct prefix keys -> cache miss cost increases (lock contention + recompute). coalescing reduces distinct prefixes.

Nina: pushed a small patch locally that groups tokens until min_bytes or token_end then writes a single frame. code change is ~20 LOC, bench harness attached.

Elaine: also looked at gRPC vs raw HTTP2 handler differences — gRPC layer was doing an extra copy for each incoming DATA chunk which amplifies the cost. recommend bypass copy when frame_size > threshold.

Ryan: are there any security/semantics concerns with coalescing? chunk boundaries sometimes used by streaming apps.

Sanjay: we should preserve application-visible token boundaries when explicit (e.g., explicit flush event). only coalesce implicit small tokenizer emissions. add unit-test to ensure semantic parity.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 1799991210 -> noted p99 increase, auto-rollback configured.

Elaine: opened PR #3124: "ingress: coalesce small token frames and avoid per-chunk copy in grpc path". bench numbers and profiler attached in PR description. cc @eng-runtime for review.

Marc: follow-ups:
- metric: frames_per_request (histogram)
- metric: avg_frame_size
- kv: prefix_miss_rate per request
- alert: sudden rise in frames_per_request or kv prefix miss rate

Nina: will run canary with coalesce=256B and copy-bypass in grpc. schedule tonight.

Ryan: also add check for http2 max_frame_size interactions and windowing; ensure we don't starve flow control.

Sanjay: +1 to metrics and safe defaults. after canary if numbers look good we can roll to prod.

Elaine: thanks all — will post final canary results here. :white_check_mark:
